Rashi on Gittin 48a:10:1.hebrew: ר' מאיר אומר - בהקדישה בחיי אביו זו אינה שדה אחוזה, וחוזרת לו מחמת אביו שמכרה לו; וקרא כי אתא, למת אביו ואחר כך הקדישה אתא:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:10:1.english: Rabbi Meir says - [If he consecrated it during his father's lifetime,] this [field] is not an ancestral field, and it reverts to him [in the Jubilee] on account of his father who sold it to him; and when the verse comes, it comes for [the case where] his father died and afterward he consecrated it:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:10:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: ואילו לר' יהודה ור' שמעון, מת אביו ואח"כ הקדישה לא צריך קרא, מאי לאו בהא קמיפלגי כו' - ולא גרסינן הכא "אלא לאו דאזלי בתר פדיון", ובמס' ערכין (דף יד:) גרסינן לה:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:10:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: "Whereas according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, [if] his father died and afterward he consecrated it, no verse is needed; what, is it not about this that they disagree, etc." - And we do not read here "rather, is it not that they follow [the time of] redemption," [for] in Tractate Arakhin (14b) we read it:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:10:3.hebrew: לא צריכא קרא - דאי צריכא קרא, הקדישה ואח"כ מת אביו, מנא להו:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:10:3.english: A verse is not required - For if a verse were required [for that case], from where would they [derive the case where] he consecrated it and afterward his father died?

Rashi on Gittin 48a:11:1.hebrew: קנין פירות - שהיתה קנויה לו מאביו בשעה שמת אביו, וקנין פירות הוא, שהרי היובל נוהג:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:11:1.english: Acquisition of produce - For [the field] had been purchased by him from his father at the time his father died, and it is [an] acquisition of produce, since the Jubilee [year] applies:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:11:2.hebrew: כקנין הגוף דמי - וכי מיית אביו לא ירית מידי ולא הויא ליה אחוזה; הלכך, אי לאו דרבייה קרא, לא הוה אמינא דתיהוי כשדה אחוזה, ואצטריך קרא למת אביו ואחר כך הקדישה:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:11:2.english: Is like acquisition of the [land] itself - And when his father dies, he does not inherit anything and it is not [considered] an ancestral [field] for him; therefore, had the verse not included it, I would not have said that it is like an ancestral field, and a verse is needed for [the case where] his father died and afterward he consecrated it:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:12:1.hebrew: לאו כקנין הגוף דמי - וכי מית אביו, ירית גופא; הלכך מת אביו ואחר כך כו':
Rashi on Gittin 48a:12:1.english: [Acquisition of produce] is not like acquisition of the [field] itself - And when his father dies, he inherits the [field] itself; therefore, [if] his father died and afterward [he consecrated it], etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:12:2.hebrew: כקנין הגוף דמי - ומודו דמת אביו ואחר כך הקדישה, צריכא קרא:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:12:2.english: Is like acquisition of the item itself - And they [Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Shimon] agree [with Rabbi Meir] that [in a case where] his father died and afterward he consecrated it, a verse is necessary:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:13:1.hebrew: והכא קרא אשכחו ודרוש - לרבויי מינה אף הקדישה ואחר כך מת אביו, דאם כן דלא מרבי אלא מת אביו ואחר כך הקדישה:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:13:1.english: And here they found a verse and expounded [it] - To include from it even [the case where] he consecrated it and afterward his father died; for if [it were] so, that it only includes [the case where] his father died and afterward he consecrated it:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:13:2.english: Let the verse write “which is not his ancestral field” - and not write “of [the] field”:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:14:1.hebrew: לקוחות הן - דאין ברירה, והוי כמו שהחליפו חלקיהן:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:14:1.english: They are purchasers - because there is no retroactive designation [bereirah], and it is as though they exchanged their portions:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:14:2.hebrew: ומחזירין ביובל - משום מצות יובל, וכיון דאמר ירושה המתחלקת הויא לקיחה, אם אית ליה קנין פירות — דהיינו כל לקיחה שבשעת יובל — לאו כקנין הגוף דמי, ואין מביא וקורא:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:14:2.english: And they return [their portions] in the Jubilee - because of the mitzvah of the Jubilee, and since he says [that] an inheritance that is divided is [considered] a purchase, if he holds [that] ownership of produce — which is [the status of] every purchase at a time when the Jubilee [is in effect] — is not like ownership of the land itself, then [one] does not bring [first fruits] and recite [the declaration]:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:15:1.hebrew: לא משכחת - מביא וקורא, אלא בירושה שלא נחלקה משנפלה בימי יהושע, דהיינו חד בר חד — שלא היו לו ולאביו ולכל הדורות למפרע עד יהושע שני בנים לאיש אחד שיחלקו ירושה:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:15:1.english: You will not find - [one who] brings [first fruits] and recites [the declaration], except with an inheritance that was never divided since it fell [to the family] in the days of Joshua — that is, an only [son], the son of an only [son] — where neither he, nor his father, nor any of the generations going back to Joshua had two sons to one man who would divide [the] inheritance:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:1:1.hebrew: בזמן שהיובל נוהג - כל מכירת קרקע לפירות, שהרי חוזר הגוף ביובל:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:1:1.english: At a time when the Jubilee is practiced - every sale of land [is only] for [its] produce, since the land itself returns in the Jubilee [year]:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:3:1.english: He descended with the intention [of acquiring] the produce - and not with the intention of acquiring the land even [for] one hour:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:6:1.hebrew: הקונה שני אילנות בתוך שדהו של חבירו - דקי"ל בבבא בתרא (דף פא.) דלא קנה קרקע, הלכך אינו קורא, דלא מצי למימר "פרי האדמה אשר נתת לי":
Rashi on Gittin 48a:6:1.english: One who acquires two trees in another’s field - For it is an established law for us in Bava Batra (81a) that he does not acquire land; therefore he does not recite [the declaration], because he cannot say, "the fruit of the ground that You have given me":

Rashi on Gittin 48a:6:2.english: But [if he acquires] three - [he brings and recites,] for we hold that he acquires the land beneath them, between them, [and around them] to the extent of a gatherer and his basket:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:6:3.hebrew: מביא וקורא - ואע"ג דהדרא ביובל:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:6:3.english: He brings [the first fruits] and recites [the verses] - Even though [the land] returns in the Jubilee [Year]:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:7:1.english: Dispute - of Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yochanan:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:7:2.hebrew: ביובל שני - שמנו ישראל, שכבר הורגלו להחזיר קרקעות, בההיא קאמר ריש לקיש "מביא ואינו קורא", דסמכא דעתיה דמוכר דודאי הדרא ליה, וזה הלוקח בטוח שיחזירנה:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:7:2.english: During the second Jubilee - that Israel counted, when they had already become accustomed to returning lands — in that [case] Reish Lakish says, "[He] brings [the first fruits] and does not recite [the verses]," for the seller relies [on the fact] that it will certainly return to him, and this [buyer] is certain that he will return it:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:7:3.english: [During the first Jubilee] - All these mishnayot [refer to] the first Jubilee:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:8:1.english: [Let us say it is] like [a dispute between] Tannaim - [Namely, whether] ownership of produce is like ownership of the principal or not:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:8:2.hebrew: שדה אחוזה - אם הקדישה ולא גאלה קודם היובל, ומכרה גיזבר לאחר, אינה נגאלת עוד, וכשהיא יוצאה ביובל מיד הלוקחה מן הגזבר, מתחלקת לכהנים, שנא' (ויקרא כ״ז:כ׳): "ואם לא יגאל את השדה וגו' והיה השדה בצאתו וגו'". ושדה מקנה — כשהקדישה ולא גאלה, ומכרה הגזבר, כשהיא יוצאה ביובל, חוזרת לבעלים הראשונים שמכרוה למקדיש, שנאמר: "בשנת היובל ישוב השדה לאשר קנהו מאתו וגו'":
Rashi on Gittin 48a:8:2.english: An ancestral field - If one consecrated it and did not redeem it before the Jubilee [Year], and the [Temple] treasurer sold it to another [person], it can no longer be redeemed; and when it goes out in the Jubilee [Year] from the hand of the one who purchased it from the treasurer, it is divided among the priests, as it is stated (Leviticus 27:20): "And if he will not redeem the field, etc., and the field, when it goes out, etc." Whereas an acquired field — when one consecrated it and did not redeem it, and the treasurer sold it, when it goes out in the Jubilee [Year], it returns to the original owners who sold it to the consecrator, as it is stated: "In the year of the Jubilee, the field shall return to him from whom he bought it, etc.":

Rashi on Gittin 48a:8:3.hebrew: מניין ללוקח שדה מאביו והקדישה - בחיי אביו, בעודה בידו שדה מקנה:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:8:3.english: From where [is it derived] regarding one who purchases a field from his father and consecrated it - [He consecrated it] during his father's lifetime, while it was [still] in his possession [as] a purchased field:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:8:4.english: And afterward his father died - and it became an ancestral [field] for him:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:8:5.hebrew: מניין שתהא לפניו כשדה אחוזה - אם לא גאלה ומכרה הגזבר, שיוצאה לכהנים ביובל:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:8:5.english: From where [is it derived] that it should be before him like an ancestral field - [Meaning that] if he did not redeem it and the [Temple] treasurer sold it, it goes out to the priests in the Jubilee [Year]:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:9:1.english: Which is not of the field of his possession - It is a superfluous verse:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:9:2.hebrew: שדה שאינה ראויה - בשעה שהקדישה, להיות לו שדה אחוזה לעולם:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:9:2.english: A field that is not fit - [not fit] at the time he consecrated it to be an ancestral field for him forever:

Rashi on Gittin 48a:9:3.hebrew: יצתה זו כו' - וכל שכן מת אביו ואחר כך הקדישה, דבשעת הקדש כבר היתה אחוזה:
Rashi on Gittin 48a:9:3.english: This [field] is excluded, etc. - And all the more so [if] his father died [first] and afterward he consecrated it, for at the time of consecration it was already an ancestral [field]:

Tosafot on Gittin 48a:13:1.hebrew: לא דכ"ע קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי - דיחויא בעלמא הוא, דרבי יהודה אית ליה בהחובל (ב"ק דף צ.) גבי דין יום או יומים, דלאו כקנין הגוף דמי:
Tosafot on Gittin 48a:13:1.english: No, [rather] everyone [holds that] acquisition of produce is like acquisition of the body [itself] - This is merely a deflection, for Rabbi Yehuda holds in [the chapter entitled] Haḥovel (Bava Kamma 90a), regarding the law of "a day or two," that [acquisition of produce] is not like acquisition of the body [itself]:

Tosafot on Gittin 48a:14:1.hebrew: אי לאו דאמר ר' יוחנן קנין פירות כו' - הקשה רבינו תם: ואנו איך מצאנו ידינו ורגלינו? דקיימא לן כריש לקיש דלאו כקנין הגוף דמי, כדאמרינן בריש החולץ (יבמות דף לו:), וקיימא לן נמי דבדאורייתא אין ברירה, דבסוף מסכת ביצה (דף לח.) פסקינן כרבי אושעיא, ורב נחמן דקיימא לן (כתובות יג.) כוותיה בדיני — ואמרינן בריש פרק ב' דקדושין (דף מב:): "האחים שחלקו הרי הן כלקוחות, פחות משתות נקנה מקח", ופסקינן נמי בהמוכר את הבית (ב"ב דף סה.) דאין להן דרך זה על זה, דמוכר בעין רעה מוכר, אלמא לקוחות הן! והא דפסקינן בפ' בית כור (בבא בתרא דף קז.) כרב דאמר "בטלה מחלוקת" — לאו משום דיורשין הוו, אלא משום דהוו כלקוחות באחריות; ויורשין דקאמר רב, לאו יורשין ממש, אלא כלומר כיורשין, וברוב ספרים גרסינן הכי בפרק קמא דבבא קמא (דף ט.). ומיהו רב אסי דאמר "יחלוקו" ומספקא ליה אי יורשין הוו — היינו יורשין ממש, כדמוכח בפרק יש בכור (בכורות דף מח.) גבי "חמש ולא חצי חמש"; ורבי אסי אמר רבי יוחנן "האחין שחלקו לקוחות הן" — לאו היינו רב אסי, אי נמי הא דידיה הא דרביה. והא דפסקינן בנדרים בפרק השותפין (נדרים דף מו:) כר"א בן יעקב בשותפין שנדרו הנאה זה מזה דמותר ליכנס לחצר — לאו מטעמיה, דטעמיה משום ברירה, כדמוכח בפרק הפרה (ב"ק דף נא:), אלא משום דויתור הוא כרבינא בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף נז:), ומותר במודר הנאה. וי"ל דדוקא בההיא לחודה, בהכותב לבנו מהיום ולאחר מיתה, קיימא לן כריש לקיש דלאו כקנין הגוף דמי, משום דאבא לגבי ברא אחולי מחיל, דהכי מצריך להו בפרק יש נוחלין (בבא בתרא דף קלו:) לתרי מילי דריש לקיש דהכא ודהתם; אבל בעלמא קיימא לן דכקנין הגוף דמי. ואף על גב דקאמר הכא רבא "קרא ומתניתא מסייעי ליה לריש לקיש" — לרבא לא סבירא ליה הכי, דאם לא כן לא מצא ידיו ורגליו, דרבא סבר לקוחות הן בפרק ב' דקדושין (דף מב:); ובפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מח.) קאמר רבא נמי גבי משיכה מפורשת מן התורה "קרא ומתניתא מסייעי ליה לריש לקיש", אף על גב דרבא קאי כר' יוחנן בר מתלת (יבמות דף לו.). ועי"ל דדוקא רבי יוחנן אית ליה דמחזירין זה לזה ביובל, אבל שאר אמוראים סברי אע"ג דלקוחות הן אין מחזירין, דמכר הוא דאמר רחמנא דליהדר, ירושה ומתנה לא; והשתא אתי שפיר. וא"ת: לרבי יוחנן דמחזירין זה לזה ביובל, תו לא משכחת שדה אחוזה, דכולהו הוו שדה מקנה, ולא תתחלק לכהנים, וגם יפדוה בשוויה ולא בית זרע חומר שעורים בחמשים שקל כסף? וי"ל: כיון דתחת זו תחזור לו אחרת, לא קרינן בה שדה מקנה אלא שדה אחוזה:
Tosafot on Gittin 48a:14:1.english: If not that Rabbi Yoḥanan said that the acquisition of produce, etc. - Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: And how do we find our hands and feet [in the study hall]? For we rule in accordance with Reish Lakish that [acquisition of produce] is not like acquisition of the body [of the property], as we say at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] HaCholetz (Yevamot 36b); and we also rule that in Torah law there is no retroactive clarification, for at the end of tractate Beitzah (38a) we rule in accordance with Rabbi Oshaya; and [as for] Rav Naḥman, whom we rule in accordance with in monetary laws (Ketubot 13a) — we say at the beginning of the second chapter of Kiddushin (42b): "Brothers who divided [an inheritance] are like purchasers; [if the discrepancy is] less than a sixth, the acquisition takes effect," and we also rule in [the chapter entitled] HaMokher Et HaBayit (Bava Batra 65a) that they do not have a right of way over each other, because one who sells, sells with a stingy eye — thus, they are [considered] purchasers! And that which we rule in the chapter [entitled] Beit Kor (Bava Batra 107a) in accordance with Rav, who says "the division is void" — [that is] not because they are [considered] heirs, but rather because they are like purchasers with a guarantee; and "heirs" that Rav says does not mean actual heirs, but rather "like heirs," and in most texts we read it thus in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (9a). However, [as for] Rav Asi, who says "they divide" and is in doubt whether they are heirs — that means actual heirs, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 48a) regarding "five [selas], and not half of five"; and Rabbi Asi who said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, "Brothers who divided are [considered] purchasers," is not the same [person as] Rav Asi — or alternatively, that [statement] is his own [view], and this [statement] is his teacher's [view]. And that which we rule in Nedarim in the chapter [entitled] HaShutafin (Nedarim 46b) in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov regarding partners who vowed not to derive benefit from each other, that [each] is permitted to enter the courtyard — [that is] not for his reason, for his reason is because of retroactive clarification, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] HaParah (Bava Kamma 51b), but rather because it is a waiver, like Ravina in [the chapter entitled] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 57b), and it is permitted for one who is barred by a vow from benefit. And one can answer that specifically in that [case] alone, of one who writes [a gift of his property] to his son "from today and after death," we rule in accordance with Reish Lakish that it is not like acquisition of the body, because a father toward a son readily waives [his rights], for thus [the Gemara] requires them in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 136b) for the two statements of Reish Lakish, here and there; but in general, we rule that it is like acquisition of the body. And even though Rava says here, "A verse and a baraita support Reish Lakish" — Rava [himself] does not hold like that, for if so, he would not find his hands and feet, since Rava holds they are [considered] purchasers in the second chapter of Kiddushin (42b); and in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 48a) Rava also says regarding [the view that] meshikhah is explicit in the Torah, "A verse and a baraita support Reish Lakish," even though Rava stands in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan in all except three [disputes] (Yevamot 36b). And one can also answer that specifically Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that they return [the portions] to each other in the Jubilee, but the other Amoraim hold that even though they are [considered] purchasers, they do not return [them], for it is [only] a sale that the Merciful One said returns, [whereas] inheritance and gift do not; and now it works out well. And if you ask: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who [holds] that they return [the portions] to each other in the Jubilee, you will never find an ancestral field, for all of them will be a purchased field, and it will not be divided to the priests, and also they will redeem it at its [market] value and not [at the rate of] "an area for a homer of barley seed at fifty shekels of silver"? One can answer: Since in place of this one, another will return to him, we do not call it a purchased field, but rather an ancestral field:
